facts.text: I asked to proofread an email and give thoughts without changing anything in the response.
I expressed gratitude to the landlord for repairing the dishwasher in a timely manner.
Venkatesh came to take a look at the dishwasher on Monday morning.
I had meant to send a thank you email sooner but I had been very unwell that week.
I found a rusty metal spike sticking out of the ground where the back gate is to be replaced.
I heard an awful shriek from my dog and I can only assume my dog stepped on the spike.
Venkatesh informed me there was construction debris back there but never mentioned hazards coming out of the ground.
I only found the spike after hearing my dog shriek.
I had only ever seen metal posts used for construction laid flat on the ground near the gate site.
I thought the construction mess was limited to those laid-flat metal posts.
I believed the spike had been present most likely since the removal of the gate without being noticed.
This happened while my dog was in the backyard while Venkatesh was seeing to the dishwasher.
My dog is usually not outside unattended.
I had no reason to believe there was a dangerous hazard in the area.
I told Rent Select that the neighborhood has seemingly started to degrade in terms of safety.
In my entire tenancy up until recently, I had always felt very safe.
In recent months, a few neighbors have been affected by an uptick in crime and aggressive individuals in the area.
The park in the middle of the neighborhood has started to show signs of unruly individuals.
I recently had my safety threatened there by an individual I can only presume was on drugs.
I was distressed to wake up this morning and find our side gate wide open to the street.
The side gate had been secured with the latch and bolted.
Due to the gardeners coming through, my personal master lock had not been resecured on the latch.
I believed the bottom bolt on the gate (the one going into the ground) being shut the night before made it likely someone hopped the fence to open it.
I said that if there was someone casing the house, they are now aware of a large amount of technology inside.
I said the technology inside includes personal computers with expensive accessories.
I said I am worried about a break-in.
I wanted to touch base on the progress toward security cameras the landlord stated he wanted to install.
I wanted to address the security of the front and garage doors, which are both in need of repair.
Venkatesh fixed the lock on the front screen door.
We are still awaiting the main door repairs.
The wood on the actual front door is still decaying in places.
I said the active construction sites have been left in place so long that the sites and items in them are starting to show signs of decay.
I planned to attach photos of the front yard site and the backyard area where the gate is to be replaced.
The baseboard that the back gate will be sitting on shows signs of the same rot that could have contributed to the decay of the back gate.
At the front construction site, there has been rusty rebar sticking out of the ground very close to the neighbor's yard.
The actual structure Venkatesh is working to build is starting to fall apart due to weathering.
There is starting to be weed growth that I do not feel comfortable having removed from an active construction site with hazards such as rebar posts sticking out of the ground.
I was not sure if the landlord intends to conduct repairs this weekend.
It was currently Friday at 9 am when I wrote the letter.
I had not heard from the landlord through the course of the week aside from Monday when he said he'd be in touch.
I assumed the landlord would be sorting other matters this weekend.
The landlord informed me that Saturdays are the primary days he can come to attend to the repairs.
I said I am happy to make myself available on those days.
I requested more than 24 hours notice so I can plan my weekend with certainty.
I requested that the matters involving security be expedited.
I asked where, in the proofread response, there were areas of the letter that could be tightened up for clarity.
I asked for a copy of the letter with appropriate changes for all but the 3rd dot point in the response.

events.text: Venkatesh repaired the dishwasher after inspecting it on Monday morning.
I found a rusty metal spike sticking out of the ground where the back gate is to be replaced after hearing my dog shriek.
I woke up to find the side gate wide open to the street.
It was Friday at 9 am when I wrote that I had not heard from the landlord through the week aside from Monday.
I requested repairs on Saturdays and more than 24 hours notice for weekend planning.
